newsitem.title: GERMANY: German call money edges up to 3.07/3.10 percent.
newsitem.headline: German call money edges up to 3.07/3.10 percent.

text.p: German call money rates edged up to 3.07 to 3.10 percent on Tuesday as liquidity conditions tightened slightly at several banks due to shifts of funds by public authorities, dealers said.

Dealers also said they did not have the slightest hope that the Bundesbank would ease its securities repurchase, or repo, rate at its council meeting on Thursday, adding that, in any case, there was no justification for a repo cut.
Bank deposits with the Bundesbank increased on Monday to 40.4 billion marks from 39.7 billion marks on Friday while the monthly average was unchanged at 40 billion.
Borrowings at the Lombard window rose to 300 million marks from a negligible level on Friday.
The Frankfurt Interbank Overnight Average was at 3.10333 percent vs 3.09633 percent.
